description: V2 retrieval baseline corpus: realistic native repository memories and labelled queries.

memories.content: The governed review mutation path must apply the decision and its memory status change atomically in one SQLite transaction; retry after a crash must remain possible.
Review previews are bound to a revision and idempotency token so a stale approval cannot mutate a changed subject.
The function apply_review_mutation is the native owner of governed review writes in src/memory/storage/sqlite_memory_database.cpp.
A failed durable capture must leave a retryable job; a completed claim is recorded only after the write commits, so worker recovery cannot lose work.
The 2025 capture incident involved a worker acknowledging a memory before its transaction completed; recovery then skipped the missing claim.
Code snapshots are whole-snapshot generations. A loaded snapshot is stale until a successful scan, and source fingerprints must be checked before current code enters context.
The old code index used name-only function IDs and could silently select the last same-name target.
Current release work uses the main branch and requires a clean native build before merging.
The alpha repository builds with PlatformIO and C++17 using the native environment.
Historical release work used the develop branch before the repository moved to main.
The current policy keeps build caches disposable and never treats generated artifacts as source evidence.
An earlier cache policy treated generated build output as reusable evidence for debugging.
The retry incident led to the atomic capture decision; the decision is documented in the recovery runbook.
The beta repository builds with Meson and Clang; its release branch is stable.
Beta review approvals use a separate service and do not share alpha's SQLite mutation path.
Never place passwords or private absolute paths in durable memory; redact them before persistence.

queries.query: Before editing the governed review write path, how do I preserve all-or-nothing status changes?
Which build toolchain is used for this repository?
Which recovery decision followed the capture incident?
What is the current release branch policy?
What is the approved cache policy for source evidence?
When can a code snapshot be trusted after source edits?
What sensitive data must never be stored in memory?
